coverage: Existing Isaac rotor control and measured replay

findings.finding: Aerodynamic drag depends on relative air velocity squared, density and effective coefficient-area. A pressure-centre offset also creates a moment. These relations support a bounded seeded wind experiment; implementing the full Dryden spectrum would be a separate fidelity decision.
findings.relevance: Demonstrating controller stabilization under repeatable turbulent wind in the existing PhysX drone
findings.direction_alignment: The maintainer explicitly requested turbulence simulation and a stabilization demonstration after merging rotor control.
findings.opportunity_or_risk: A same-wind reference isolates horizontal feedback. Calling a simple temporal OU process a validated atmospheric model would overstate fidelity.
findings.engineering_cost: One wind/control comparison slice, strict versioned evidence, measured GPU trials and local visualization
findings.roadmap_delta: AL-007 turbulence stabilization precedes the previously proposed takeoff/contact slice
findings.verification_needed: Force/moment and seed tests, same-source paired PhysX trials, recovery gates, evidence tampering checks and browser comparison

overall_recommendation: Add the requested bounded temporal wind with explicit drag and paired horizontal-feedback ablation. Preserve the existing gains and baselines.
evidence_gaps: Illustrative drag area and pressure centre are not calibrated against hardware
No Dryden/Von Karman spectral or outdoor-weather validation is claimed
